_comment: Stanford MyHealth template. To complete: log into MyHealth.Stanford.edu, open DevTools, follow the discovery procedure in tools/v3/README.md (or use tools/v3/runtime/discover_portal.js to capture endpoints automatically), and replace each TODO with the captured value. Per C-017 this is the path to recover Stanford's ~165 unscraped clinical notes (the IsClinicalNoteAvailable=True visits from stanford_visits_raw.json).
name: Stanford MyHealth

auth._comment: The anti-forgery-token pattern is universal across Epic-based portals. Verify by inspecting any XHR request from MyHealth in DevTools Network tab.

visits._comment: UCSF uses Epic.PatientAccess.Components.__Instances[7]. Stanford's number may differ — run discover_portal.js to find it. Stanford's Visits page may also paginate via 'Load more past visits' (or similar wording); set button_text below if so.

paginator.button_text: TODO: e.g. 'load more past visits' if Stanford uses similar pagination

endpoint._comment: Stanford's visit-detail endpoint path may differ from UCSF's. To find: click a visit in the UI; in DevTools Network tab note the POST that returns the visit details JSON; copy its path here, and inspect the body to confirm the fields below match.
endpoint.path: TODO: e.g. /api/visits/past-details/GetVisitDetailsPast — verify in Network tab

notes._comment: Stanford's note-content endpoint analogous to UCSF's LoadReportContent. Same discovery procedure: click a visit with a note, expand the note, capture the POST.

filter._comment: If Stanford's response shape matches UCSF's, the same filter works. If not, adjust the paths.

endpoint.path: TODO: e.g. /api/report-content/LoadReportContent — verify in Network tab
